second_checker.tool: nanoda (nanoda_bin of toolchain lean-4.35.0-windows, input from leanexport)
second_checker.command: leanexport <module> -- <theorem> > export.ndjson; nanoda_bin config.json (permitted_axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; unpermitted_axiom_hard_error, nat_extension, string_extension true)
second_checker.procedure: one theorem per run; the export contains the theorem and every declaration it depends on, including the Lean core and Mathlib declarations; LEAN_PATH as given by lake env; a run is stopped when a process exceeds 4 GiB of private memory or 30 minutes; the export file is removed after each run
second_checker.note: every run printed "Checked N declarations with no typechecker errors, 1 pretty printer errors: [Unable to print axioms]"; the pretty printer error concerns the printing of the axiom list, not type checking. leanexport needed 3275 to 4014 MiB of private memory, nanoda_bin at most 512 MiB; export files 26 to 212 MB.

statements.name: Theorem 1 (residual enclosure)
statements.correspondence: Document: for Hermitian A, x != 0 and real mu some eigenvalue satisfies |lambda - mu| <= ||Ax - mu x||/||x||. Lean: the same over RCLike (real or complex), x in EuclideanSpace with the Euclidean norm, eigenvalues hA.eigenvalues (Mathlib's unsorted indexing). No difference beyond the field being any RCLike field.

statements.name: Theorem 1, multi-pair form used by S2
statements.correspondence: Document: every claimed pair gets its own interval; distinctness is not claimed (two copies of one vector share an eigenvalue). Lean: a function f from the pair index to eigenvalue indices with each bound; f is not claimed injective.

statements.name: Theorem 1 with the S1 model shift sigma
statements.correspondence: Document: radius add_up(r, sigma) for the eigenvalues of H with ||H - A|| <= sigma. Lean: radius ||Ax - mu x||/||x|| + sigma for the eigenvalues of Hermitian H, with the hypothesis either pointwise (||(H - A)v|| <= sigma ||v|| for all v) or as Mathlib's spectral norm ||H - A|| <= sigma (scope Matrix.Norms.L2Operator). Proved by the triangle inequality and Theorem 1 for H; the outward rounding of add_up is not part of the statement.

statements.name: Floating-point model: standard model, INT-05 additive term, directed rounding; Higham Lemmas 3.1 and 3.3, sums in any order, dot product and matrix-vector bounds, complex product (Higham Lemma 3.5)
statements.source: Higham 2002 Lemmas 3.1, 3.3, 3.5 and eqs. (3.4), (3.11); code/certify-ed/docs/proofs/int05_underflow.md model M-U and Lemma U1; certify_ed/fp.py add_up, sub_down
statements.correspondence: The model is a structure of hypotheses on an abstract rounding rnd on a normed group V (R or C): every result is representable, |rnd z - z| <= u|z| + eta for every exact result z (INT-05 model M-U), and sums of representable numbers carry no absolute term. Binary64 fixes u = 2^-53, eta = 2^-1075 and adds monotonicity and the neighbours succ, pred used by add_up and sub_down (outward_interval). Lemma 3.1 is stated for a list of factors (1 + delta)^(+-1); Lemma 3.3 as the inequalities gamma_k + u(1 + gamma_k) <= gamma_(k+1), gamma_j + gamma_k + gamma_j gamma_k <= gamma_(j+k), c gamma_k <= gamma_(ck), gamma_k + u <= gamma_(k+1)(1 - u). A sum in any order and association is a binary tree (STree); comp_error bounds the computed tree sum for leaf errors gamma_a|t| + beta, which gives the dot product bound gamma_k sum|a_i b_i| + k(1 + gamma_(k-1)) eta (U1) and, with eta = 0, the row bound |fl(Ax)_i - (Ax)_i| <= gamma_w (|A||x|)_i. For complex data, crnd rounds both components and cmul forms (ac - bd) + i(ad + bc) from four rounded real products and two rounded sums; cmul_err is |fl(ab) - ab| <= gamma_3 |ab| (from sqrt(2) gamma_2 <= gamma_3, proved as 2(2u + u^2)^2 <= (3u)^2).

statements.name: Theorem 1 floating-point accounting, real data
statements.source: code/certify-ed/docs/proofs/thm1_fp-accounting.md; certify_ed/enclosure.py residuals, _rounding_bound; certify_ed/fp.py gamma, norm2_upper, norm2_lower
statements.correspondence: The computation of residuals is modelled operation by operation: y_i as the rounded products A_ij x_j summed along a tree T_i with at most w leaves covering the stored entries of row i, R_i = fl(y_i - fl(x_i mu)), the bound E_i = fl(fl(fl(fl(fl(a_i / fl(1 - gamma_hat_(w+1))) (1 + 4u)) + fl(|x_i||mu|)) gamma_hat_(w+2)) (1 + 4u)) with a_i the computed |A||x| along a second tree and gamma_hat_k = fl(ku / fl(1 - ku)) (fp.gamma, ku exact), norm2_upper and norm2_lower with fl(||v||) = fl(sqrt(sum of rounded squares along a tree over all entries)), the factors fl(1 +- gamma_hat_(n+2)), the guard 1 + 8u and arbitrary nonnegative tails, and rel = fl(fl(fl(fl(fl(R_up + E_up) + c1) / x_low)(1 + 4u)) + c0) with c0, c1 >= 0 (the INT-05 terms of the code). Hypotheses: standard model (eta = 0), u <= 2^-53, 1 <= w <= 2^26, n <= 2^26, x_low > 0. Conclusion: ||Ax - mu x|| / ||x|| <= rel (residual_radius_fl), and for a real symmetric matrix some eigenvalue lies within rel of mu (residual_enclosure_fl). The summation order is arbitrary; products are rounded separately (no fused multiply-add). The per-stage slack is as in the document: norm2_upper >= (1 + u)||v|| and norm2_lower <= (1 - u)||v||, which absorbs the fourth rounding of the final quotient.
statements.gap: Theorem 1 under the underflow-tolerant model (eta = 2^-1075, Lemma U5 of int05_underflow.md) is not formalized; the theorem holds in the standard model and allows the code additive terms as arbitrary nonnegative additions.

statements.name: Theorem 1 floating-point accounting, complex data
statements.correspondence: As the real case with: complex products cmul (error gamma_3), complex sums and the product x_i mu rounded componentwise, each modulus |A_ij|, |x_j|, |x_i| rounded once (hypot modelled as one rounding of the exact modulus), the computed |A||x| divided by 1 - gamma_hat_(w+3), the entrywise bound with fl(2 gamma_hat_(w+6)), the norms of complex vectors as sums of the 2n squares of the real components with the factor 1 +- gamma_hat_(n+2) of norm2_upper (n the complex length). Hypotheses: eta = 0, u <= 2^-53, 1 <= w, w + 4 <= 2^26, n <= 2^26. The complex norm bounds use sqrt(1 - g) >= 1 - g/2 - g^2/4 with g = gamma_(2n) and (nu)^2 <= u/2.

statements.name: Theorem 3 (Kato-Temple)
statements.correspondence: Document: ||x|| = 1, theta = x^H A x, r = ||Ax - theta x||, (alpha, beta) containing theta and exactly one eigenvalue lambda: theta - r^2/(beta - theta) <= lambda <= theta + r^2/(theta - alpha). Lean (kato_temple): the same, theta written as re<x, Ax> (inner_apply_self_eq_re shows it equals <x, Ax>), 'exactly one eigenvalue' as: every eigenvalue in (alpha, beta) equals lambda (multiplicity allowed). The abstract forms need only lambda in [alpha, beta], use alpha < theta for the upper and theta < beta for the lower bound, and include division-free forms that need no hypothesis on theta.

statements.name: Gershgorin for Hermitian matrices and the norm bound ||A||_2 <= ||A||_inf
statements.correspondence: Mathlib's disc theorem is stated for an eigenvalue of toLin' A over a normed field; eigenvalue_mem_gershgorin applies it to each hA.eigenvalues i through the eigenvector eigenvectorBasis i. The statement the code uses is the consequence ||A v|| <= R ||v|| (and Mathlib's spectral norm ||A|| <= R) for Hermitian A and any R >= 0 above every row sum; Lean adds the harmless hypothesis R >= 0.

statements.name: Weyl's inequality (sorted and counting forms)
statements.correspondence: Document: |lambda_j(H_spec) - lambda_j(H_h)| <= Delta for every sorted index j when ||H_h - H_spec||_2 <= Delta. Lean: the same for Mathlib's sorted eigenvalues eigenvalues₀ (decreasing order; the document's increasing order is the reversal of both sequences, which leaves the statement unchanged), with the norm hypothesis pointwise. The counting forms #{lambda(T) <= t} <= #{lambda(S) <= t + eps} and the strict form are proved first, by a Courant-Fischer dimension count.

statements.name: Appendix A, Lemmas A1 and A2 (builder rounding, symmetrisation rounding)
statements.correspondence: A monomial amplitude is modelled as fl(...fl(fl(c f1_hat) f2_hat)... fL_hat) with f_hat = fl(f) for every factor (an exact factor is a special case of the bound) over R or C; a product of a complex number with a real or purely imaginary one is one rounding of relative error u in modulus, which is the Rounding hypothesis on C. mono_error: |t_hat - t| <= gamma_2L |t|. An entry of H_ref is the computed amplitudes of its monomials S_ij summed along a tree with at most m leaves, or 0 when S_ij is empty (leak = 0 is the hypothesis that S_ij lists exactly the monomials from j to i). Lemma A1 (builder_error): |H_ref - H_spec|_ij <= gamma_(m+2L-1) (|H|_abs)_ij. Lemma A2 (symmetrised_error): for Hermitian H_spec, |fl(H_ij + conj H_ji)/2 - H_spec,ij| <= gamma_(m+2L)((|H|_abs)_ij + (|H|_abs)_ji)/2 <= gamma_(m+2L) max(...), the halving exact; the unitarily invariant part of A2 is used through schur_split (Lemma A3 row).
statements.gap: The second sentence of Lemma A1 (the computed abs_matvec(ones) and abs_rmatvec(ones) row and column sums of |H|_abs are within a factor 1 +- gamma_(m+2L-1) of the exact sums) is not formalized.

statements.name: Appendix A, Lemma A3 (||E||_2^2 <= ||E||_1 ||E||_inf <= max^2)
statements.correspondence: Document: ||E||_2 <= sqrt(||E||_1 ||E||_inf) <= max(||E||_1, ||E||_inf) for any (rectangular) E. Lean: ||E x||^2 <= R C ||x||^2 and ||E x|| <= max(R, C) ||x|| for any upper bounds R >= 0, C >= 0 on the row and column sums. The proof is the Schur test with Cauchy-Schwarz instead of the document's route through lambda_max(E^H E); the inequality is the same. With the floating-point model: Delta_builder = gamma_W sqrt(r c) bounds ||H_ref - H_spec||_2 (builder_shift) and ||fl(H_hat) - H_spec||_2 (symmetrised_shift) for W >= m + 2L and r, c upper bounds of the row and column sums of |H|_abs; the symmetrised case uses schur_split (|M_ij| <= kappa (P_ij + P_ji) gives ||M||_2 <= 2 kappa sqrt(r c), by splitting M into two parts bounded by P and by its transpose).

statements.name: Appendix A, Theorem A4 (the model shift Delta)
statements.correspondence: model_shift_fl: ||(H_h - H_spec) x|| <= (max(R, C) + gamma_W sqrt(r c)) ||x|| with R, C bounds of the row and column sums of D = H_h - H_ref, H_ref built as in Lemma A1, W >= m + 2L, r, c bounds of the exact row and column sums of |H|_abs; weyl_transfer_fl composes it with Theorem A5 for the sorted eigenvalues.
statements.gap: The code-level evaluation (computed r and c from abs_matvec(ones), the rounding of up(g sqrt(row col)/(1 - gamma(width))(1 + 4u)), inf_norm_upper of the computed D) is not formalized; the theorem takes r, c, R, C as upper bounds.

statements.name: Appendix A, Theorem A5 (Weyl transfer for S2 and S3)
statements.correspondence: Document: (S2) an enclosure of radius r for H_h becomes one of radius r + Delta for H_spec at the same sorted index, so a matching to distinct indices stays a matching; (S3) #{lambda(H_h) < sigma - beta} <= nu <= #{lambda(H_h) <= sigma + beta} becomes the same with beta + Delta. Lean: both, with the S2 part for a family of claims mapped to sorted indices of eigenvalues₀; S4 (separations shrink by 2 Delta) is not stated separately; it follows from the S2 part.

statements.name: Polar-factor lemma (a) to (d)
statements.correspondence: Document: M = G^(1/2), Q = X M^-1 with G = X^H X, ||G - I|| = eta < 1: (a) Q^H Q = I, (b) ||M - I|| <= delta and ||M^-1|| <= (1 - eta)^(-1/2), (c) ||X - Q|| <= delta, (d) ||AQ - Q Lambda|| <= rho. Lean: X a linear map F -> E, G given by <Xu, Xv> = <Gu, v>, M and M^-1 built in an orthonormal eigenbasis of G; (a) is stated as norm preservation ||Qz|| = ||z|| (inner products are preserved too, polarQ_inner in ClusterPrime.lean); the norms in (d) are any upper bounds nR, nA >= 0, nLambda; the hypothesis 0 <= eta is added (eta is a norm in the document).

statements.name: Kahan's inclusion theorem (general Hermitian block)
statements.correspondence: Document: Q with orthonormal columns, H Hermitian with eigenvalues theta_j, r = ||AQ - QH||: g distinct indices with |lambda_{i_j} - theta_j| <= r. Lean: Q an isometry, eigenvalues of A and H sorted; the conclusion is a strictly increasing (so injective) index map, which is stronger. Step 1 (interval lemma) is the document's; Step 2 replaces Hall's marriage theorem by an explicit greedy order-preserving matching on the real line.

statements.name: Theorem 2 (clusters, radius rho)
statements.correspondence: Document: X n x g, eta = ||X^H X - I|| < 1, Lambda Hermitian with eigenvalues mu_j, R = AX - X Lambda, delta = 1 - sqrt(1 - eta), rho = ||R|| + (||A|| + ||Lambda||) delta: g distinct indices with |lambda_{i_j} - mu_j| <= rho. Lean (cluster_enclosure): X : Matrix n m, Lambda : Matrix m m Hermitian, the norm hypotheses pointwise with any upper bounds nR, nA >= 0, nLambda (as the manuscript allows), 0 <= eta added; the conclusion pairs Mathlib's sorted eigenvalues eigenvalues₀ of Lambda with those of A through a strictly increasing index map.

statements.name: Theorem 2' (sharper radius eps*) and min(rho, eps*)
statements.correspondence: Document: eps* = ||R||/sqrt(1 - eta) + ||X^H R||/(1 - eta) + delta spread(Lambda)/sqrt(1 - eta), g distinct indices within eps*; min(rho, eps*) is a valid common radius. Lean: the same with upper bounds nR >= 0 and nXR >= 0 on ||R|| and ||X^H R|| (X^H R written as the matrix Xᴴ * (A * X - X * Λ) or the adjoint of X applied to R), and spread(Lambda) replaced by hi - lo for any lo <= mu_j <= hi (equal to the document's for lo = mu_min, hi = mu_max). cluster_min takes the two matchings and returns one with radius min(rho, eps*).

statements.name: E-05 variational certificates
statements.correspondence: Lemma 1 (lambda_min <= theta <= lambda_max), Lemma 2 (an eigenvalue within r of theta, which is Theorem 1 at mu = theta, and r^2 = <psi, H^2 psi>/<psi, psi> - theta^2) and Proposition 1 (Temple: theta < rho <= lambda_2 gives lambda_1 >= theta - r^2/(rho - theta)) are kernel-checked; 'rho <= lambda_2' is written as 'at most one eigenvalue, counted with multiplicity, is below rho'. Lemmas 3 and 4 (floating-point enclosure of theta and r, MPS contraction error) and Lemma 5 (Rayleigh quotient of the source state) are not formalized. Lemma 5 is rayleigh_perturb: for a symmetric T with ||T z|| <= n_H ||z||, n_H >= 0, and ||psi - psi_hat|| <= e < ||psi_hat||, |theta(psi) - theta(psi_hat)| <= (2 ||T psi_hat - theta_hat psi_hat|| e + (n_H + |theta_hat|) e^2)/(||psi_hat|| - e)^2, the first term being 2 r(psi_hat)||psi_hat|| e. From Lemma 3: (i) the numerator, |N_hat - <psi, H psi>| <= e_N + gamma_w |psi|^T |H| |psi| for y = fl(H psi) with rows of at most w entries and the exact_dot contract |N_hat - <psi, y>| <= e_N (rayleigh_numerator_bound, real data); (iii) the quotient lies between the extreme corner quotients (quotient_mem_corners).
statements.gap: Lemma 3: the computed bound E_N with fl(|psi|^T a_hat)(1 + gamma_(n+2))/(1 - gamma_(w+1)) and its guard, the outward 4u of the corners, r_stored and the rounding of the Temple bound (v), and complex data; Lemma 4 (MPS contraction) is not formalized.

statements.name: D-02 matrix-free residual bounds
statements.correspondence: Theorem D-02 (a): every contribution is a chain of products from the exact coupling with stored factors of relative error gamma_(e_l) (e_l = 0 exact letter, 1 rounded amplitude), each product rounded (real, error gamma_1) or formed by cmul (complex, gamma_3), then multiplied by the source entry; at most w_row contributions are summed along a tree. matrixfree_entry_error: |fl(Hx)_i - (H_spec x)_i| <= gamma_(w_row + L + rho)(|H_spec|_abs |x|)_i = gamma_(W-1)(...), W = w_row + L + rho + 1; matrixfree_entry_error_c: gamma_(w_row + 3L + rho + 2) = gamma_(W-1), W = w_row + 3L + rho + 3. Lemma N: ||(A (x) B) x|| <= a b ||x|| for pointwise bounds a, b (norm_kronecker_le, via A (x) B = (A (x) 1)(1 (x) B)), a diagonal sign factor preserves norms, a product of operators is bounded by the product of bounds and sum_t c_t O_t by sum_t |c_t| n_t.
statements.gap: Lemma M1 (at most w_row contributions per output entry) enters as the size of the summation tree. Part (b), the Theorem 1 radius with adapter.width = W - 2, is not formalized: with |fl(Hx) - H_spec x| <= gamma_(W-1)|H_spec||x| the residual error is <= (gamma_(W-1) + u(1 + gamma_(W-1))) a + (2u + u^2) q and the code bound gives gamma_W s (1 - u)^5 (1 + 4u) a with s = (1 - g)(1 - u)^2(1 + 4u)/((1 - g(1 - u)^2)(1 + u)) and g = gamma_(W-1); exact rational evaluation (u = 2^-53, W = 3, 10, 1000, 2^20, 2^26) gives a margin of about W u^2, so (b) holds by a second-order margin, not by the spare index the document mentions; a Lean proof needs that second-order inequality. Lemma M3 (the second pass), the reverse inequality ||A (x) B|| >= ||A|| ||B|| of the Kronecker identity and the rounding of norm_bound() are not formalized.

statements.name: E-03 generalized eigenproblems (Cholesky reduction)
statements.correspondence: Lemma 2 of E-03 (|lambda - mu| <= ||Ax - mu Bx||_{B^-1}/||x||_B <= ||Ax - mu Bx||_2/(sqrt(beta_c) ||x||_B) for 0 < beta_c <= lambda_min(B)) is kernel-checked for the eigenvalues of C = L^-1 A L^-H, with B = L L^H for an invertible L (Cholesky in the document; any invertible L in Lean), ||L^-1 s|| standing for ||s||_{B^-1} and ||L^H x|| = ||x||_B (norm_sq_adjoint_eq), and lambda_min(B) >= beta_c written as beta_c ||w||^2 <= w^H B w for all w. Of Lemma 1, C Hermitian and 'an eigenpair (y, lambda) of C gives the pencil eigenpair (L^-H y, lambda)' are kernel-checked; the converse, that the pencil eigenvalues (roots of det(A - lambda B)) are exactly those of C with multiplicity, is not. The converse half of Lemma 1 is stated for matrices: with B = L L^H, L invertible and C = L^-1 A L^-H, det(A - X B) = det B (-1)^n charpoly C as polynomials (pencil_det_eq_charpoly), so the roots of det(A - X B) with multiplicity are the eigenvalues of the Hermitian C (pencil_roots_eq_eigenvalues), and a pencil eigenpair (x, lambda) gives the eigenpair (L^H x, lambda) of C (reduced_eigenpair_of_pencil).
statements.gap: Lemma 3 (inertia of A - sigma B) and Propositions 1 to 3 (Bunch-Kaufman, floating point) are not formalized.

statements.name: Lemma 17 (dyadic exp and ln enclosures)
statements.correspondence: Integers stand for grid points k 2^-P; Python floor and ceiling division by a positive integer are the floor and ceiling of the real quotient. Proved for any P and N: (i) from_fraction encloses its argument; (ii) the grid product with the four corner products rounded outward, and the squaring step of a nonnegative interval; (iii) the floor-rounded and ceiling-rounded Taylor terms bound 2^P tau^k/k! from below and above, so (S_N_lo(t), S_N_hi(t) + rem) contains exp(t 2^-P) for 0 <= t <= 2^P (remainder from Real.exp_bound, 2 tau^(N+1)/(N+1)! for tau <= 1), s squarings give exp(2^s y), which with t_lo <= x/2^s <= t_hi gives exp(x 2^-P) for x >= 0, and the reciprocal step gives x < 0; (iv) the lower atanh sum A_lo(u) 2^-P <= log(1 + x) - log(1 - x) for x = u 2^-P < 1, and log m = log(1 + x) - log(1 - x) for x = (m - 1)/(m + 1).
statements.gap: Not formalized: the upper atanh sum with the tail term ceil(ceil(8 pw_(M+1)/7)/(2M+3)), the decomposition with k ln 2 and the enclosure of ln 2, the halving identity ceil(ceil(a/b)/c) = ceil(a/(bc)), the quotient X/Y of (ii), and (v) the conversion to binary64.

trust_note: Every theorem listed is level K: kernel-checked by the build, no sorry, admit or native_decide, axioms printed. Every module, and the root module, was replayed and accepted by leanchecker (three runs, see second_checker), so every theorem is at least K+. Level K2 means that the theorem, exported with all its dependencies by leanexport, was accepted by the independent kernel nanoda; nanoda was run on the main theorems of each statement (field main) and a statement is K2 when all its main theorems were accepted. A theorem that is only used inside an accepted export is still listed as K+.
